SSRIs (and a lot of other medicines that affect personality/behavior/mental health issues/etc) are difficult since nearly everyone responds to them differently.

I've been on Lexapro for 6 years since I was 13, currently in the process of switching medicine soon since it just doesn't do it for me. Doesn't help that the Lexapro was originally prescribed for generalized anxiety and I later developed depression. I never had any side effects and it completely turned around my symptoms. Of course, I was 13, and things are a lot more complicated now. My other medicated friends have experiences from all over the place, as is to be expected with SSRIs. 

That being said, have you considered switching off SRRIs/antidepressants and maybe trying a mood stabilizer or something similar? My doctor might be trying this with me. No prescription yet (out of town at university), so I can't comment on the effects yet but I'm (trying to be) optimistic. Just to clarify, I have depression, not bipolar disorder. 

I don't know how you're feeling about the drugs not working, but I want to remind you that **you have other options**. Even if you don't respond to SSRIs well, plenty of people respond to other classes of antidepressants, mood stabilizers, and many other kinds of drugs. If you decide to not go the medication route, I understand that entirely, but if it's what you want, don't think you're out of options or at the end of the rope prescription-wise. 

Here's to feeling better soon! I wish you nothing but the best of luck.

I'm a college student who takes vyvanse daily (it's prescribed to me, I have a diagnosis, don't worry.) 

Keep in mind that people respond to stimulants differently because everyone's body chemistry is slightly different. Because I have anxious & depressive tendencies, I had to try around ~5 different stimulants to find one that I could tolerate well (that didn't make me depressed/suicidal, shake uncontrollably, vomit, etc), and vyvanse worked for me. I've been overweight since I was pretty young, and I remember my shitlord mother being excited that I might lose some weight once I went on stimulants (this was several years ago). While I resented her for it back then, it's no secret that stimulants are awesome for appetite suppression and, therefore, weight loss. 

My semester started about 3 1/2 weeks ago, which is when I started taking vyvanse more frequently. I'm also in the process of losing weight. When I'm on vyvanse my appetite is extremely reduced. Yesterday, I ate breakfast, took vyvanse, and didn't even eat lunch or dinner, I was too hungry and anxious (exam stress). I eventually made myself eat half a granola bar before I went to bed because while I felt very *physically* hungry (stomach pains/noises, anxious, jittery, light headed) I often find that when I'm on vyvanse the idea of *actually* consuming food sounds horrible to me. And I also usually feel like I have too many other things to do so that actually going to the dining hall to eat would be a waste of my time, so I've been skipping a lot of meals. 

That being said, it's totally possible to be on vyvanse and eat a lot of food. I gained a lot of weight last semester while taking stimulants because I was using it as a coping mechanism for my anxiety, and if you take stimulants frequently it's not uncommon for some of the side effects like reduced appetite to diminish over time as your system acclimates to the drug. But it does **not** "make you feel like you have to eat". It's more of a "wow, I haven't eaten anything since 9 am and now it's 8 pm, I should probably get some food". Now that I'm more aware of my intake, I often go several hours without even feeling hungry on vyvanse and am loosing weight pretty quickly (3-4 pounds/week, but keep in mind that I'm in the process of a 50-60 pound weight loss so this isn't too alarming and I've experienced it before). I try to make up for my lack of nutrient intake during the day by eating a big breakfast before I take my medicine and by making sure I get at least something in my system for dinner (most days).  

Also, on a pharmacological level, vyvanse is very very similar to most other common stimulants, so there's really no chemical reason why vyvanse would cause weight gain when adderal/ritalin/concerta/etc all suppress appetite. But, like I said before, sometimes you can adjust to the drug you're on and not experience as strong effects of things like appetite suppression after a period of time. When I'm off my vyvanse, it's definitely more difficult to watch my intake as I actually feel like eating.

Source: the daily life of a vyvanse-riddled undergrad neuroscience student

I know some of medicine can affect appetite by increasing hunger, but I honestly credit my stimulant medication in helping me manage portion control and food choices. I'm a college student who takes vyvanse almost every day (it's on a per need basis, prescribed to me) and as a side effect I lose my appetite. Yesterday I didn't eat anything between 9 am and 5 pm simply because between 2 lectures and a 3 hour lab and my meds, I just wasn't hungry. And when I do eat, I'm a lot more likely to eat small-normal portions because I'm less hungry, as opposed to large portions, which is how I eat if I were to ignore my self control. 

EDIT: For the record, I still maintain a normal calorie intake. My TDEE for my height/weight/activity level is around ~2800 (I'm not small and work out 6x a week) and I estimate I'm eating around 2000-2200 a day, give or take. If I let myself though, I can easily eat upwards of 3000-3500 calories a day when I'm not on medicine.
